extraction.Name: Julia Goings
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not want her patent in fee to her 320 acre allotment at the time she received it, September 29, 1919, but that the Indian Agency told her, if she did not take the patent, and pay the taxes, it would be taxed just the same, for which it would later be sold, so she accepted the patent
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: in 1926, she sold her place to a Mr. Collier, of Kadoka, South Dakota, for $1300.00 cash
extraction.Buyer: Mr. Collier, of Kadoka, South Dakota, for $1300.00 cash
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: got behind in the taxes, and Mr. Collier paid the back taxes, which amounted to $688.00
extraction.Occupation/Income: her husband does some gardening, besides working at common labor whenever he can get it to do; and that this constitutes their only income
extraction.NOTES: mentally incompetent; health is not good, being bothered with rheumatism and kidney trouble; she and her husband have two minor children and six grand children to support, all of whom have good health; husband has good health; she considers she received a poor price for her land, it being good soil, with running water and timber on it; did not sell her land for any debts incurred prior to receiving her patent in fee; has never received any aid from the County, State nor the United States Government; document number No. 5460; sworn March 7, 1929 | TASK 5 BULK ALLOTMENT RECOVERY 2026-04-29: Sonnet text-extraction captured the allotment number from the source page header but classified it in NOTES as a 'document number' / 'Document No.' / 'No. NNNN' instead of placing it in the structured Allotment number field. The hypothesis that these document/file references are actually allotment numbers was confirmed via BLM cross-reference (exemplars: Eugene Means 2249, Lucy Patton 6802). This patch corrects 48 records via bulk regex extraction from NOTES with user-supervised review of every HIGH-confidence proposal.

recovery_notes.rationale: Source page header contained 'No. NNNN' which Sonnet captured in NOTES as 'document number' rather than placing in structured Allotment field. Hypothesis confirmed via BLM cross-reference.
